bull_bear.body: Prioritizing organic capacity expansion and R&D (new engines, EV). No M&A mentioned. Strong free cash flow generation (INR 108cr in 9M) supports self-funded growth. Dividend policy not explicitly discussed but historically consistent.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Monsoon/Liquidity: SFM segment highly sensitive to rainfall and rural credit conditions (SPARSH scheme disruptions cited as prior headwind). 2) Competition: Chinese imports (though banned in tillers, present in weeders) and global players entering India. 3) Execution: Delay in establishing Europe base or US tariff volatility. 4) Concentration: 90% of tractor exports to Europe.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and constructive. CEO labeled 'Impactful Turnaround' by ET India. Emphasizes 'structural' rather than 'cyclical' growth, dismissing competition fears by highlighting service/warranty moat. Transparent about cost disadvantages but firm on pricing power via value proposition.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 1) Caste dynamics: Management explicitly cited social barriers preventing small farmers from accessing custom hiring centers, driving ownership demand. 2) Retail Finance Inflection: 12-13% of SFM sales now via retail finance (vs near-zero previously), unlocking the bottom-of-pyramid demand. 3) Marine Adjacency: Testing compact inboard engines for fishing trawlers with zero capex commitment, leveraging existing engine R&D.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dominant market share in the Indian power tiller market, built on over five decades of experience and strong brand trust
- Extensive distribution network of 1,400+ dealers, 8,500+ retailers and 160+ spare parts distributors, plus 23 sales offices and 15 stock yards across India
- Diversified product portfolio spanning 2 HP to 50 HP - power tillers, weeders, reapers, tractors, implements, spares, electric pumps, aggregates, diesel engines and precision components
- Pioneer of the 4WD compact tractor segment in India (first launched 1982) and the first company to introduce 30 HP tractors in the Indian tractor industry
- Debt-free balance sheet with robust cash flows and liquid reserves supporting expansion
- In-house R&D and design capability - CII Design Excellence Award-winning products and R&D execution strengthened through CCPM implementation
- Global technology partnerships - Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (Japan), Kukje Machinery (Korea), Zetor Tractors and HTC Investments (Czech Republic), Pubert India
- Export presence in over 40 countries built since 1978, with the VST FIELDTRAC brand engineered to meet stringent EU standards
- Frugal innovation - delivering high-value products at affordable prices for small and marginal farmers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Monsoon and agri-cycle dependence — Tractor and Small Farm Machine demand remain monsoon-dependent, creating demand volatility. Management states near-term industry demand will continue to be influenced by monsoon performance, crop price realisation and rural liquidity conditions, resulting in periodic fluctuations in demand patterns.
- Availability of retail financing for customers — The easy availability of retail financing continues to be a significant market challenge. VST's customer base of small and marginal farmers relies on retail finance and EMI schemes, which the Company facilitates through tie-ups with banks and NBFCs; constrained credit availability directly restricts adoption of mechanised solutions.
- Technology disruption and pace of product transition — Rapid technological change risks customer disengagement without agile execution. The Company is simultaneously funding internal-combustion, electric drivetrain (SoEL) and Stage V / TREM-V compliant platforms, and the Power Tiller Industry's transition to TREM-V emission norms requires certified engines to sustain the business.
- Intensifying domestic and global competition — Escalating global and domestic competition demands continuous innovation and excellence. VST's position rests on a dominant power tiller share and compact-tractor leadership, both of which are contestable by larger tractor OEMs and imported compact machines.
- Product quality and safety liability — Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a risk: faulty products could lead to accidents, legal issues, reputational damage and loss of consumer trust. Mitigated by adherence to strict product safety regulations during design and development.
- Supply chain and supplier ESG exposure — Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a risk: effective sourcing and managing ESG risks within the supply chain are vital; failure can result in legal penalties, reputational harm and supply chain disruptions affecting long-term sustainability. Mitigated through a Supplier Risk Management and Mitigation (SRMM) process, supplier capacity development and a supplier code of conduct with ESG parameters.
- Climate change and GHG / energy dependence — Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a risk: VST depends on non-renewable fuel and energy; climate change poses risks such as reduced agricultural productivity, extreme weather costs, changing market demands and regulatory changes, while physical risks like floods, droughts and heatwaves could disrupt operations. This is a double exposure because the Company's end customers are farmers whose incomes are themselves climate-sensitive.
- Employee attrition and talent retention — The permanent-employee turnover rate was 33.62% in FY 2025-26 (39.67% in FY 2024-25), a structurally high level for an engineering manufacturer investing in in-house R&D, digital engineering and a new Global Technology Centre.
- Geographic and market concentration — Exports contributed 7% of total turnover, so results are overwhelmingly tied to the Indian farm-equipment cycle. The Company operates a single reported segment ('Manufacturing of Agricultural Machineries'), and international demand was softer during the year, particularly in Europe.
- Industrial relations at manufacturing plants — Union settlements at the Hosur and Mysuru plants have been concluded, while discussions with the union at the Malur plant are currently in progress - an unresolved settlement at a plant that produces power tillers, the Company's largest volume category.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The deck frames the company across a farm-equipment product set of Power Tiller, Tractors (Domestic and Export), Power Weeder and Power Reaper, i.e. a mechanisation portfolio broader than tractors alone.
- A 'VST ZETOR TRACTOR' product/brand is called out on its own slide, indicating a branded tractor line, though the deck gives no further detail on it.
- The company sells both in the domestic market and via exports, with tractor exports disclosed as a separate volume line from domestic tractors.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Macro - monsoon] The deck flags 'Uneven Monsoon & Rural Demand', citing a below-normal monsoon outlook and uneven rainfall distribution as a demand risk.
- [Input costs] The deck flags 'Commodity Cost Inflation', naming an inflationary trend in steel, forging, casting, aluminium and copper prices, with natural rubber prices 'elevated/volatile'.
- [Geopolitical / supply chain] The deck flags 'Geopolitical & Supply Chain Disruptions', specifically the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, driving higher crude oil, fuel, freight, insurance and logistics costs.
- [Slide-title inconsistency] The macro section is headed 'Macro Economy - Its impact in FY 25' while the presentation is dated 13-August-2026 and reports Q1 FY27; the deck is not internally consistent on the period the macro commentary covers.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Established in 1967 through a collaboration with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Japan, VST is the flagship company of the VST Group and is headquartered in Bengaluru. It manufactures and trades power tillers, power weeders, brush cutters, multi-crop reapers, compact and higher-horsepower tractors, precision components and allied agricultural implements, spares, lubricants and electric pumps. Its businesses span Small Farm Machines, Tractors, International Business, Distribution, Precision Components and Implements, serving small and marginal farmers, orchard and vineyard growers, commercial haulage users and, through its Precision Components Division, external industrial customers.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Small Farm Machines:** Power tillers (9-16.5 HP), Power weeders (2-8 HP, FR & RR), Ranger series 50 and 80 power weeders, Brush cutter, Power reaper / multi-crop reaper, Maize reaper, Electric power tillers and weeders (in development)
- **Tractors:** Classic series (17-27 HP), Series 9 (18-36 HP), FENTM series (19-30 HP), Power series (32-39 HP), VST Zetor series (40-50 HP), Viraaj series (40-50 HP), VST Shakti 270 MT HT, 95 DI Ignito
- **International Business:** VST FIELDTRAC tractors (17-50 HP), Power tillers, Power weeders, Multi-crop reapers
- **Distribution Business:** Genuine spare parts, Lubricants, Electric pumps, High-technology agricultural blades
- **Precision Components:** Precision machined components, Rotary tillers, Sprayers, Aggregates, Diesel engines

latest_quarter.body: Gross margins vary by product; blended GM estimated 30-35%. Admitted 15-20% cost disadvantage vs Chinese imports, offset by 2-year warranty, service network, and brand trust. Copper price volatility noted for radiators but deemed immaterial; ferrous metal inflation stable. Operating leverage from volume surge drove Op EBITDA expansion to 12.9%.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: FY26 full year expected 25-30%. Margins: Comfortable maintaining current levels (~13% Op EBITDA) despite 15-20% cost disadvantage vs Chinese imports due to value-added service/warranty. Order Inflow: Strong traction in SFM; Tractor exports to stabilize in Q4. Capex: ~INR 60cr cash outflow in FY27 for capacity expansion and global tech center.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Management did not disclose specific order book numbers; emphasized 'normal year' organic demand driven by retail finance penetration (12-13% of SFM sales) and last-mile distribution expansion rather than bulk government orders.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) Distribution Depth: Scaling from 1,000 to 6,000 counters (Taluka level) to capture the 10 crore un-mechanized households. 2) Product Mix: Launch of FENTM engine tractors and revamped Zetor series in Q4/FY27. 3) Geography: Direct subsidiary in Europe (Netherlands) by Q1 FY27 to improve working capital rotation; US market re-entry targeted for 2027. 4) New Verticals: Marine engine pilot phase; Electric tillers/weeders seeding from March 2026.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Evolve power tillers into a broader Small Farm Machines portfolio and expand globally, addressing the mechanisation needs of small and marginal farmers
- Scale retail presence from 1,000 to 5,000 counters to ensure taluka-level product availability
- Subject to demand scale-up and channel expansion, evaluate calibrated capacity enhancement including potential manufacturing footprint expansion in northern and western markets
- Maintain and strengthen leadership in the compact tractor segment through efficient, application-focused and differentiated new models, expanding across priority markets including Gujarat and Maharashtra
- Over the next four years, introduce enhanced compact tractor offerings through the development of global platforms, scaling volumes and improving utilisation of tractor manufacturing capacity
- Maximise higher-horsepower (40-50 HP) manufacturing capacity utilisation through the VST Zetor joint venture with HTC Investments and Zetor Tractors, strengthening dealer and finance partnerships particularly across northern India
- Promote precision components and implements - expand the Precision Components Division beyond captive supply into external customers across automotive, locomotive, defence, industrial equipment, electric vehicles, aerospace and marine engines, leveraging global China-plus-one sourcing shifts
- Expand rural distribution into an integrated omnichannel network connecting distributors, retailers, digital platforms and service partners, and scale adjacent rural-product categories
- Participate in technology evolution - develop a diversified product pipeline spanning internal-combustion and electric technologies, with the SoEL (Source Electric) initiative developing electric drivetrain platforms for tractors and Small Farm Machines
- Establish a Global Technology Centre at Hosur for end-to-end new product development, strengthening in-house R&D and reducing dependence on external resources
- Evaluate an operational base in Europe to improve fulfilment resilience, and prepare for a phased entry into the United States as the regulatory and tariff environment evolves
- Continue to spend on R&D to innovate and bring new solutions for the small and marginal farmer segment
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: VST operates three manufacturing units in southern India (Hosur, Mysuru and Malur) alongside 23 sales offices, 15 stock yards and an experience centre at Pune. The largest disclosed expansion project is a Global Technology Centre at Hosur, being established with a phased investment of approximately Rs 100 crore, intended to provide end-to-end new product development covering engineering, electric powertrains, battery technologies, testing and validation and digital product development across tractors and small farm machinery, strengthening in-house R&D and reducing dependence on external resources. On manufacturing capacity, the Company states that subject to demand scale-up and channel expansion it will evaluate calibrated capacity enhancement, including potential manufacturing footprint expansion in northern and western markets - no site, quantum or timeline is committed. In higher-horsepower tractors, capacity utilisation is being lifted through VST Zetor Private Limited, the joint venture with Czech manufacturer Zetor Tractors a.s. and its parent HTC Investments a.s., established with a share capital of Rs 19 Crore (VST 51%, HTC 49%); a revamped VST Zetor 40-50 HP range was launched in Q4 FY 2025-26 after an extensive market-seeding programme, with dealer, distribution and finance partnerships being expanded particularly across northern India. In compact tractors the Company plans, over the next four years, to introduce enhanced offerings through the development of global platforms, scaling volumes and improving utilisation of existing tractor manufacturing capacity. Distribution capacity is being expanded from 1,000 to 5,000 retail counters for taluka-level availability, with the network having reached 165 distributors and 8,545 retailers. Internationally, VST incorporated VST Americas Inc and VST FieldTrac LLC (both yet to commence operations), is evaluating an operational base in Europe to improve fulfilment resilience, and remains prepared for a phased entry into the United States as the regulatory and tariff environment evolves. The Mysuru plant obtained AS 9100:2016 certification for aerospace and defence parts manufacturing during the year, extending the Precision Components Division into new end markets.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Long-term outlook for agricultural mechanisation remains positive, driven by increasing mechanisation, growing policy support for small and marginal farmers, and the need to improve farm productivity
- Near-term industry demand will continue to be influenced by monsoon performance, inflationary trends and global developments
- The Power Tiller Industry will transition to TREM-V emission norms; the Company states its engines are ready with certification to sustain the business
- Structural shift towards compact, affordable and application-specific equipment: nearly 86% of Indian operational holdings measure less than two hectares, with average operational holding size estimated at 1.08 hectares, limiting the economic viability of large farm equipment
- Smallholdings of less than 5 hectares accounted for 51.42% of the agricultural machinery market in 2025, underlining the importance of compact mechanisation solutions
- Government initiatives under the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation (SMAM), subsidies, custom-hiring models and improving access to retail finance are supporting adoption of agricultural machinery
- Institutional support remains strong - agricultural credit disbursements reached Rs 28.69 Lakh Crore in FY 2024-25, and cumulative PM-KISAN transfers exceeding Rs 4.09 Lakh Crore have been made to more than 11 Crore farmers, supporting rural liquidity and farmers' investment capacity
- Gross irrigated area increased from 41.7% to 55.8% of gross cropped area, supporting multi-cropping and increasing the intensity of agricultural operations
- Rising rural incomes, labour shortages, growing agricultural exports and changing cropping practices are accelerating adoption of mechanised solutions across farm sizes and crop categories
- The Indian agricultural machinery market was valued at USD 18.15 Billion in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 19.65 Billion in 2026, projected to expand to USD 29.27 Billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 8.28% during 2026-2031
- The Indian tractor industry recorded wholesale sales crossing the one-million-unit mark for the first time in FY 2025-26, supported by favourable monsoon, improved rural liquidity, policy support and GST reductions on tractors and certain farm inputs
- The global agricultural tractor market was valued at USD 67.5 Billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 105.5 Billion by 2033, a CAGR of 5.8% during 2026-2033
- International demand was softer, particularly in Europe, where demand was largely driven by replacement purchases and adoption of technologically advanced tractors with precision farming, GPS-enabled systems and telematics; African markets present long-term growth opportunities given low mechanisation levels
- For FY 2026-27 real GDP is expected to grow between 6.8% and 7.2% and inflation is expected to normalise towards around 4.4%, supporting household consumption and rural demand
- Easy availability of retail financing continues to be a significant market challenge; tractor and SFM demand remain monsoon-dependent, creating demand volatility
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: VSTL delivered a blowout Q3 with 44% revenue growth and 3x PAT, driven by a structural turnaround in domestic small farm machinery (SFM) and tractors, while operational leverage expanded margins despite commodity headwinds. The thesis shifts from cyclical recovery to sustained structural growth as the company scales its retail network to 6,000 counters and prepares for direct European operations and US market re-entry.

currentContext.expansion: VST operates three manufacturing units in southern India (Hosur, Mysuru and Malur) alongside 23 sales offices, 15 stock yards and an experience centre at Pune. The largest disclosed expansion project is a Global Technology Centre at Hosur, being established with a phased investment of approximately Rs 100 crore, intended to provide end-to-end new product development covering engineering, electric powertrains, battery technologies, testing and validation and digital product development across tractors and small farm machinery, strengthening in-house R&D and reducing dependence on external resources. On manufacturing capacity, the Company states that subject to demand scale-up and channel expansion it will evaluate calibrated capacity enhancement, including potential manufacturing footprint expansion in northern and western markets - no site, quantum or timeline is committed. In higher-horsepower tractors, capacity utilisation is being lifted through VST Zetor Private Limited, the joint venture with Czech manufacturer Zetor Tractors a.s. and its parent HTC Investments a.s., established with a share capital of Rs 19 Crore (VST 51%, HTC 49%); a revamped VST Zetor 40-50 HP range was launched in Q4 FY 2025-26 after an extensive market-seeding programme, with dealer, distribution and finance partnerships being expanded particularly across northern India. In compact tractors the Company plans, over the next four years, to introduce enhanced offerings through the development of global platforms, scaling volumes and improving utilisation of existing tractor manufacturing capacity. Distribution capacity is being expanded from 1,000 to 5,000 retail counters for taluka-level availability, with the network having reached 165 distributors and 8,545 retailers. Internationally, VST incorporated VST Americas Inc and VST FieldTrac LLC (both yet to commence operations), is evaluating an operational base in Europe to improve fulfilment resilience, and remains prepared for a phased entry into the United States as the regulatory and tariff environment evolves. The Mysuru plant obtained AS 9100:2016 certification for aerospace and defence parts manufacturing during the year, extending the Precision Components Division into new end markets.

risks.note: Tractor and Small Farm Machine demand remain monsoon-dependent, creating demand volatility. Management states near-term industry demand will continue to be influenced by monsoon performance, crop price realisation and rural liquidity conditions, resulting in periodic fluctuations in demand patterns.

risks.risk: Availability of retail financing for customers
risks.note: The easy availability of retail financing continues to be a significant market challenge. VST's customer base of small and marginal farmers relies on retail finance and EMI schemes, which the Company facilitates through tie-ups with banks and NBFCs; constrained credit availability directly restricts adoption of mechanised solutions.

risks.risk: Technology disruption and pace of product transition
risks.note: Rapid technological change risks customer disengagement without agile execution. The Company is simultaneously funding internal-combustion, electric drivetrain (SoEL) and Stage V / TREM-V compliant platforms, and the Power Tiller Industry's transition to TREM-V emission norms requires certified engines to sustain the business.

Escalating global and domestic competition demands continuous innovation and excellence. VST's position rests on a dominant power tiller share and compact-tractor leadership, both of which are contestable by larger tractor OEMs and imported compact machines.

Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a risk: faulty products could lead to accidents, legal issues, reputational damage and loss of consumer trust. Mitigated by adherence to strict product safety regulations during design and development.

risks.risk: Supply chain and supplier ESG exposure
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a risk: effective sourcing and managing ESG risks within the supply chain are vital; failure can result in legal penalties, reputational harm and supply chain disruptions affecting long-term sustainability. Mitigated through a Supplier Risk Management and Mitigation (SRMM) process, supplier capacity development and a supplier code of conduct with ESG parameters.

risks.risk: Climate change and GHG / energy dependence
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a risk: VST depends on non-renewable fuel and energy; climate change poses risks such as reduced agricultural productivity, extreme weather costs, changing market demands and regulatory changes, while physical risks like floods, droughts and heatwaves could disrupt operations. This is a double exposure because the Company's end customers are farmers whose incomes are themselves climate-sensitive.

The permanent-employee turnover rate was 33.62% in FY 2025-26 (39.67% in FY 2024-25), a structurally high level for an engineering manufacturer investing in in-house R&D, digital engineering and a new Global Technology Centre.

Exports contributed 7% of total turnover, so results are overwhelmingly tied to the Indian farm-equipment cycle. The Company operates a single reported segment ('Manufacturing of Agricultural Machineries'), and international demand was softer during the year, particularly in Europe.

Union settlements at the Hosur and Mysuru plants have been concluded, while discussions with the union at the Malur plant are currently in progress - an unresolved settlement at a plant that produces power tillers, the Company's largest volume category.

one-line thesis: VSTL delivered a blowout Q3 with 44% revenue growth and 3x PAT, driven by a structural turnaround in domestic small farm machinery (SFM) and tractors, while operational leverage expanded margins despite commodity headwinds. The thesis shifts from cyclical recovery to sustained structural growth as the company scales its retail network to 6,000 counters and prepares for direct European operations and US market re-entry.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 314cr (+44% YoY); 9M: INR 912cr (+32%). EBITDA Margin: 12.9% (vs 8.9% YoY), aided by volume leverage and labor code provisioning normalization. PAT: INR 30.7cr (vs INR 1.7cr YoY); YoY comp distorted by prior year mark-to-market losses. Order Book: Not disclosed, but management cites 'normal year' demand with no special government orders driving the 55% SFM volume spike. Net Debt: Improved cash generation of INR 108cr in 9M; balance sheet remains net cash positive.
guidance: Revenue Growth: FY26 full year expected 25-30%. Margins: Comfortable maintaining current levels (~13% Op EBITDA) despite 15-20% cost disadvantage vs Chinese imports due to value-added service/warranty. Order Inflow: Strong traction in SFM; Tractor exports to stabilize in Q4. Capex: ~INR 60cr cash outflow in FY27 for capacity expansion and global tech center.
order book & pipeline: Management did not disclose specific order book numbers; emphasized 'normal year' organic demand driven by retail finance penetration (12-13% of SFM sales) and last-mile distribution expansion rather than bulk government orders.
segment / subsidiary detail: Power Tillers: 12,545 units Q3 (+85% YoY on low base); 9M: 37,374 (+55%). Power Weeders: 3,429 units Q3 (+108%); 9M: 8,399 (+63%). Domestic Tractors: 32% growth in Q3; 9M: 3,352 (+18%). Exports: Tractor exports 320 units Q3 (-16%); 9M: 886 (-23%), but negativity reducing. Power Reapers: Seasonal taper in Q3.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Distribution Depth: Scaling from 1,000 to 6,000 counters (Taluka level) to capture the 10 crore un-mechanized households. 2) Product Mix: Launch of FENTM engine tractors and revamped Zetor series in Q4/FY27. 3) Geography: Direct subsidiary in Europe (Netherlands) by Q1 FY27 to improve working capital rotation; US market re-entry targeted for 2027. 4) New Verticals: Marine engine pilot phase; Electric tillers/weeders seeding from March 2026.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margins vary by product; blended GM estimated 30-35%. Admitted 15-20% cost disadvantage vs Chinese imports, offset by 2-year warranty, service network, and brand trust. Copper price volatility noted for radiators but deemed immaterial; ferrous metal inflation stable. Operating leverage from volume surge drove Op EBITDA expansion to 12.9%.
capex / expansion: FY27 cash capex guided at ~INR 60cr. Focus on doubling power weeder capacity (current 70k, expandable to 100k via 3rd shift), potential new greenfield plant in North/West India (under evaluation), and Global Tech Center. Marine segment requires no dedicated capex (third-party marinization).
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic capacity expansion and R&D (new engines, EV). No M&A mentioned. Strong free cash flow generation (INR 108cr in 9M) supports self-funded growth. Dividend policy not explicitly discussed but historically consistent.
risks & watch-items: 1) Monsoon/Liquidity: SFM segment highly sensitive to rainfall and rural credit conditions (SPARSH scheme disruptions cited as prior headwind). 2) Competition: Chinese imports (though banned in tillers, present in weeders) and global players entering India. 3) Execution: Delay in establishing Europe base or US tariff volatility. 4) Concentration: 90% of tractor exports to Europe.
management quality / tone: Highly confident and constructive. CEO labeled 'Impactful Turnaround' by ET India. Emphasizes 'structural' rather than 'cyclical' growth, dismissing competition fears by highlighting service/warranty moat. Transparent about cost disadvantages but firm on pricing power via value proposition.
non-obvious takeaways: 1) Caste dynamics: Management explicitly cited social barriers preventing small farmers from accessing custom hiring centers, driving ownership demand. 2) Retail Finance Inflection: 12-13% of SFM sales now via retail finance (vs near-zero previously), unlocking the bottom-of-pyramid demand. 3) Marine Adjacency: Testing compact inboard engines for fishing trawlers with zero capex commitment, leveraging existing engine R&D.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: VST Tillers Tractors Limited is one of India's leading manufacturers of power tillers and a pioneer of 4WD compact tractors, offering farm-mechanisation solutions from 2 HP to 50 HP across more than 40 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1967 through a collaboration with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Japan, VST is the flagship company of the VST Group and is headquartered in Bengaluru. It manufactures and trades power tillers, power weeders, brush cutters, multi-crop reapers, compact and higher-horsepower tractors, precision components and allied agricultural implements, spares, lubricants and electric pumps. Its businesses span Small Farm Machines, Tractors, International Business, Distribution, Precision Components and Implements, serving small and marginal farmers, orchard and vineyard growers, commercial haulage users and, through its Precision Components Division, external industrial customers.

(49%) to manufacture and sell 40-50 HP tractors developed for Indian farming requirements. Does not participate in the BRSR initiatives of the listed entity.
- VST Americas Inc. (VST America INC) — subsidiary: 100% held by the listed entity; incorporated in 2024 and yet to commence operations. Does not participate in the BRSR initiatives of the listed entity.
- VST FieldTrac LLC — subsidiary: 100% held by the listed entity; incorporated in 2024 and yet to commence operations. Does not participate in the BRSR initiatives of the listed entity.
- HTC Investments a.s. — JV: Joint venture partner holding 49% of VST Zetor Private Limited; parent company of Zetor Tractors a.s. and owner of the Zetor brand.
- Zetor Tractors a.s. — JV: Czech tractor manufacturer and joint venture partner in VST Zetor Private Limited, providing the premium higher-horsepower tractor range for India.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Small Farm Machines:** Power tillers (9-16.5 HP), Power weeders (2-8 HP, FR & RR), Ranger series 50 and 80 power weeders, Brush cutter, Power reaper / multi-crop reaper, Maize reaper, Electric power tillers and weeders (in development)
- **Tractors:** Classic series (17-27 HP), Series 9 (18-36 HP), FENTM series (19-30 HP), Power series (32-39 HP), VST Zetor series (40-50 HP), Viraaj series (40-50 HP), VST Shakti 270 MT HT, 95 DI Ignito
- **International Business:** VST FIELDTRAC tractors (17-50 HP), Power tillers, Power weeders, Multi-crop reapers
- **Distribution Business:** Genuine spare parts, Lubricants, Electric pumps, High-technology agricultural blades
- **Precision Components:** Precision machined components, Rotary tillers, Sprayers, Aggregates, Diesel engines

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Long-term outlook for agricultural mechanisation remains positive, driven by increasing mechanisation, growing policy support for small and marginal farmers, and the need to improve farm productivity
- Near-term industry demand will continue to be influenced by monsoon performance, inflationary trends and global developments
- The Power Tiller Industry will transition to TREM-V emission norms; the Company states its engines are ready with certification to sustain the business
- Structural shift towards compact, affordable and application-specific equipment: nearly 86% of Indian operational holdings measure less than two hectares, with average operational holding size estimated at 1.08 hectares, limiting the economic viability of large farm equipment
- Smallholdings of less than 5 hectares accounted for 51.42% of the agricultural machinery market in 2025, underlining the importance of compact mechanisation solutions
- Government initiatives under the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation (SMAM), subsidies, custom-hiring models and improving access to retail finance are supporting adoption of agricultural machinery
- Institutional support remains strong - agricultural credit disbursements reached Rs 28.69 Lakh Crore in FY 2024-25, and cumulative PM-KISAN transfers exceeding Rs 4.09 Lakh Crore have been made to more than 11 Crore farmers, supporting rural liquidity and farmers' investment capacity
- Gross irrigated area increased from 41.7% to 55.8% of gross cropped area, supporting multi-cropping and increasing the intensity of agricultural operations
- Rising rural incomes, labour shortages, growing agricultural exports and changing cropping practices are accelerating adoption of mechanised solutions across farm sizes and crop categories
- The Indian agricultural machinery market was valued at USD 18.15 Billion in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 19.65 Billion in 2026, projected to expand to USD 29.27 Billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 8.28% during 2026-2031
- The Indian tractor industry recorded wholesale sales crossing the one-million-unit mark for the first time in FY 2025-26, supported by favourable monsoon, improved rural liquidity, policy support and GST reductions on tractors and certain farm inputs
- The global agricultural tractor market was valued at USD 67.5 Billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 105.5 Billion by 2033, a CAGR of 5.8% during 2026-2033
- International demand was softer, particularly in Europe, where demand was largely driven by replacement purchases and adoption of technologically advanced tractors with precision farming, GPS-enabled systems and telematics; African markets present long-term growth opportunities given low mechanisation levels
- For FY 2026-27 real GDP is expected to grow between 6.8% and 7.2% and inflation is expected to normalise towards around 4.4%, supporting household consumption and rural demand
- Easy availability of retail financing continues to be a significant market challenge; tractor and SFM demand remain monsoon-dependent, creating demand volatility

In higher-horsepower tractors, capacity utilisation is being lifted through VST Zetor Private Limited, the joint venture with Czech manufacturer Zetor Tractors a.s. and its parent HTC Investments a.s., established with a share capital of Rs 19 Crore (VST 51%, HTC 49%); a revamped VST Zetor 40-50 HP range was launched in Q4 FY 2025-26 after an extensive market-seeding programme, with dealer, distribution and finance partnerships being expanded particularly across northern India. In compact tractors the Company plans, over the next four years, to introduce enhanced offerings through the development of global platforms, scaling volumes and improving utilisation of existing tractor manufacturing capacity. Distribution capacity is being expanded from 1,000 to 5,000 retail counters for taluka-level availability, with the network having reached 165 distributors and 8,545 retailers. Internationally, VST incorporated VST Americas Inc and VST FieldTrac LLC (both yet to commence operations), is evaluating an operational base in Europe to improve fulfilment resilience, and remains prepared for a phased entry into the United States as the regulatory and tariff environment evolves. The Mysuru plant obtained AS 9100:2016 certification for aerospace and defence parts manufacturing during the year, extending the Precision Components Division into new end markets.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident and constructive. CEO labeled 'Impactful Turnaround' by ET India. Emphasizes 'structural' rather than 'cyclical' growth, dismissing competition fears by highlighting service/warranty moat. Transparent about cost disadvantages but firm on pricing power via value proposition.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Dominant market share in the Indian power tiller market, built on over five decades of experience and strong brand trust
- Extensive distribution network of 1,400+ dealers, 8,500+ retailers and 160+ spare parts distributors, plus 23 sales offices and 15 stock yards across India
- Diversified product portfolio spanning 2 HP to 50 HP - power tillers, weeders, reapers, tractors, implements, spares, electric pumps, aggregates, diesel engines and precision components
- Pioneer of the 4WD compact tractor segment in India (first launched 1982) and the first company to introduce 30 HP tractors in the Indian tractor industry
- Debt-free balance sheet with robust cash flows and liquid reserves supporting expansion
- In-house R&D and design capability - CII Design Excellence Award-winning products and R&D execution strengthened through CCPM implementation
- Global technology partnerships - Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (Japan), Kukje Machinery (Korea), Zetor Tractors and HTC Investments (Czech Republic), Pubert India
- Export presence in over 40 countries built since 1978, with the VST FIELDTRAC brand engineered to meet stringent EU standards
- Frugal innovation - delivering high-value products at affordable prices for small and marginal farmers

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Monsoon/Liquidity: SFM segment highly sensitive to rainfall and rural credit conditions (SPARSH scheme disruptions cited as prior headwind). 2) Competition: Chinese imports (though banned in tillers, present in weeders) and global players entering India. 3) Execution: Delay in establishing Europe base or US tariff volatility. 4) Concentration: 90% of tractor exports to Europe.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: 1) Caste dynamics: Management explicitly cited social barriers preventing small farmers from accessing custom hiring centers, driving ownership demand. 2) Retail Finance Inflection: 12-13% of SFM sales now via retail finance (vs near-zero previously), unlocking the bottom-of-pyramid demand. 3) Marine Adjacency: Testing compact inboard engines for fishing trawlers with zero capex commitment, leveraging existing engine R&D.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve power tillers into a broader Small Farm Machines portfolio and expand globally, addressing the mechanisation needs of small and marginal farmers
- Scale retail presence from 1,000 to 5,000 counters to ensure taluka-level product availability
- Subject to demand scale-up and channel expansion, evaluate calibrated capacity enhancement including potential manufacturing footprint expansion in northern and western markets
- Maintain and strengthen leadership in the compact tractor segment through efficient, application-focused and differentiated new models, expanding across priority markets …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Macro - monsoon] The deck flags 'Uneven Monsoon & Rural Demand', citing a below-normal monsoon outlook and uneven rainfall distribution as a demand risk.
- [Input costs] The deck flags 'Commodity Cost Inflation', naming an inflationary trend in steel, forging, casting, aluminium and copper prices, with natural rubber prices 'elevated/volatile'.
- [Geopolitical / supply chain] The deck flags 'Geopolitical & Supply Chain Disruptions', specifically the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, driving higher crude oil, fuel, freight, insurance and logistics costs.
- [Slide-title inconsistency] The macro section is headed 'Macro Economy - Its impact in FY 25' while the presentation is dated 13-August-2026 and reports Q1 FY27; the deck is not internally consistent on the period the macro commentary covers.

one-line thesis: VSTL delivered a blowout Q3 with 44% revenue growth and 3x PAT, driven by a structural turnaround in domestic small farm machinery (SFM) and tractors, while operational leverage expanded margins despite commodity headwinds. The thesis shifts from cyclical recovery to sustained structural growth as the company scales its retail network to 6,000 counters and prepares for direct European operations and US market re-entry.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 314cr (+44% YoY); 9M: INR 912cr (+32%). EBITDA Margin: 12.9% (vs 8.9% YoY), aided by volume leverage and labor code provisioning normalization. PAT: INR 30.7cr (vs INR 1.7cr YoY); YoY comp distorted by prior year mark-to-market losses. Order Book: Not disclosed, but management cites 'normal year' demand with no special government orders driving the 55% SFM volume spike. Net Debt: Improved cash generation of INR 108cr in 9M; balance sheet remains net cash positive.
guidance: Revenue Growth: FY26 full year expected 25-30%. Margins: Comfortable maintaining current levels (~13% Op EBITDA) despite 15-20% cost disadvantage vs Chinese imports due to value-added service/warranty. Order Inflow: Strong traction in SFM; Tractor exports to stabilize in Q4. Capex: ~INR 60cr cash outflow in FY27 for capacity expansion and global tech center.
order book & pipeline: Management did not disclose specific order book numbers; emphasized 'normal year' organic demand driven by retail finance penetration (12-13% of SFM sales) and last-mile distribution expansion rather than bulk government orders.
segment / subsidiary detail: Power Tillers: 12,545 units Q3 (+85% YoY on low base); 9M: 37,374 (+55%). Power Weeders: 3,429 units Q3 (+108%); 9M: 8,399 (+63%). Domestic Tractors: 32% growth in Q3; 9M: 3,352 (+18%). Exports: Tractor exports 320 units Q3 (-16%); 9M: 886 (-23%), but negativity reducing. Power Reapers: Seasonal taper in Q3.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Distribution Depth: Scaling from 1,000 to 6,000 counters (Taluka level) to capture the 10 crore un-mechanized households. 2) Product Mix: Launch of FENTM engine tractors and revamped Zetor series in Q4/FY27. 3) Geography: Direct subsidiary in Europe (Netherlands) by Q1 FY27 to improve working capital rotation; US market re-entry targeted for 2027. 4) New Verticals: Marine engine pilot phase; Electric tillers/weeders seeding from March 2026.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margins vary by product; blended GM estimated 30-35%. Admitted 15-20% cost disadvantage vs Chinese imports, offset by 2-year warranty, service network, and brand trust. Copper price volatility noted for radiators but deemed immaterial; ferrous metal inflation stable. Operating leverage from volume surge drove Op EBITDA expansion to 12.9%.
capex / expansion: FY27 cash capex guided at ~INR 60cr. Focus on doubling power weeder capacity (current 70k, expandable to 100k via 3rd shift), potential new greenfield plant in North/West India (under evaluation), and Global Tech Center. Marine segment requires no dedicated capex (third-party marinization).
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic capacity expansion and R&D (new engines, EV). No M&A mentioned. Strong free cash flow generation (INR 108cr in 9M) supports self-funded growth. Dividend policy not explicitly discussed but historically consistent.
risks & watch-items: 1) Monsoon/Liquidity: SFM segment highly sensitive to rainfall and rural credit conditions (SPARSH scheme disruptions cited as prior headwind). 2) Competition: Chinese imports (though banned in tillers, present in weeders) and global players entering India. 3) Execution: Delay in establishing Europe base or US tariff volatility. 4) Concentration: 90% of tractor exports to Europe.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

hero.oneLiner: VST Tillers Tractors Limited is one of India's leading manufacturers of power tillers and a pioneer of 4WD compact tractors, offering farm-mechanisation solutions from 2 HP to 50 HP across more than 40 countries.
